Kuvitus: pimeän huoneen ikkunaluukussa o: Illustration: in the shutter of a dark room there is a narrow slit, and sunlight comes through it as a beam onto a glass prism on a table. The prism spreads the light into colours from red to violet, and the colours fall on a white screen. Narrow dark lines cross the band of colours.
Kaavakuva kolmesta vedyn spektristä sama: Schematic figure of three spectra of hydrogen on the same wavelength scale, 380–720 nanometres. At the top, the continuous spectrum of an incandescent bulb: all colours from violet to red as one unbroken band. In the middle, the emission spectrum of hot, thin hydrogen gas: four bright lines on a black background at the wavelengths 410, 434, 486 and 656 nanometres. At the bottom, the absorption spectrum when continuous light passes through hot hydrogen gas, as in the atmosphere of a star: the continuous band of colours has dark lines at exactly the same wavelengths, emphasised by dashed lines. The wavelength scale is to scale.
Energiatasokaavio fluoresenssista, energ: Energy-level diagram of fluorescence, the energies to scale. At the start, the molecule of a dye is in the ground state. It absorbs an ultraviolet photon with a wavelength of 365 nanometres and an energy of 3.40 electronvolts, and moves to the excited state. In the excited state the molecule gives away part of its energy as heat in small steps and drops to the lowest level of the excited state. From there it returns to the ground state and emits a photon of visible light with a wavelength of 520 nanometres and an energy of 2.38 electronvolts. The energy of the emitted photon is smaller and its wavelength longer than those of the absorbed one.
Vetyatomin energiatasokaavio, energia-ak: Energy-level diagram of the hydrogen atom, the energy axis to scale. The levels n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 have the energies −13.6, −3.40, −1.51, −0.85, −0.54 and −0.38 electronvolts, and at the top is the energy zero, at which the electron is free of the atom. The highest levels are very close together. Four downward arrows show emission from levels 3, 4, 5 and 6 to level 2; the wavelengths of their photons, 656, 486, 434 and 410 nanometres, are marked under the arrows, and the arrows are coloured with the colour of the light. On the right, an upward arrow shows absorption from the ground state to level 2: the atom absorbs an ultraviolet photon, drawn as a wavy line, with a wavelength of 122 nanometres.
Periaatekuva kasvihuoneilmiöstä, ei mitt: Schematic figure of the greenhouse effect, not to scale, simplified. Visible light from the Sun passes through the atmosphere to the ground, because the gases of the atmosphere hardly absorb visible light. The warmed ground radiates infrared. A carbon dioxide molecule absorbs an infrared photon and then emits a new infrared photon in a random direction, here two photons: one downwards towards the ground and the other upwards and to the right towards space.
Kuva mittakaavassa: tuntemattoman lampun: Figure to scale: the emission spectrum of an unknown lamp on a black background, with a wavelength scale of 380–720 nanometres. The small tick marks of the scale are 10 nanometres apart and the numbers 50 nanometres apart. The spectrum has a violet line at about 405 nanometres, a blue one at about 436, a green one at about 546 and two close yellow lines at about 577 and 579 nanometres.
